artboards.title: Reading what was said, without leaving
The page at 1440 — one card open

annotations.text:
Issues #965 and #966 landed on the same seam from opposite sides.

#965: the card text is clipped, so you open the person — and the in-app back drops you at a bare /around with every filter reset, because state.from carries the pathname and not the search string.

#966: "I can't see the comments I posted." Reading the code, that is worse than a display gap. The page is mounted with no props, so the "Posted" toast has never once fired. markSeen then clears the accent dot. And the message itself never renders — thread items on untied contacts are dropped before they become anything.

You write something, the composer vanishes, the card gets dimmer, and nothing else happens.

OPEN — one word from you.

A contact has TWO staff threads:

· Conversation — everyone tied to the contact (they added them, they are a co-creator, they are the owner, or they keep them on their own My Day).

· Full-timers — staff only, scope: "team". Not visible to Trainees.

Around is Full-timer-only, so the strip could legitimately show either or both.

Drawn here: Conversation ONLY. It is the thread the card's composer already posts into, so what you write is what you see.

The alternative is a two-tab strip, or a merged stream with the Full-timers messages marked. Both add a control to a card that is trying to lose one — but if the Full-timers thread is where the real reasoning happens on people you are not carrying, showing only Conversation would hide the better half.

Say which and I will redraw.

Seen was passive, Completed deliberate. On Around the passive half had already stopped earning its place: the New/All filter cuts on completed, the header pill counts not-completed, and CONTEXT.md already said "opening things never makes the number fall".

Seen survived as an accent dot and a "Mark all seen" button. Both go.

The consequence to watch, recorded in ADR 0022: the count gets bigger and stickier, because it now falls only when you review something. That is the point — but if it is allowed to sit permanently high it becomes wallpaper, and the fix then is to narrow what reaches Around, not to make the count decay again.

The grid is items-start, so an open card makes its row taller and leaves its neighbours top-aligned with space beneath them.

That is the honest reason only one card opens at a time: two open cards in a 3-up row leave a ragged hole in the middle of a page you are trying to work down.

Note what has NOT changed — the day headings, the order, the dates. A posted message does not re-date or re-sort its card. "Today" means when the team touched this person.

One column, so there is no grid to keep uniform — but the collapsed clamp stays anyway, because scrolling past eight full interaction bodies to find the one you want is its own problem.

Every target is 44px. The action row stacks into two full-width primaries with the icons beneath.

The bottom nav bar is unchanged (ADR 0015 decision 7) and is omitted from the drawing.
